findings.note: FAQ item 3 says "The statute does not mention hoarding." This is an absence-of-law claim. The ledger has no statute_absence claim, so it is unproven (SR-6). Remove the sentence.

FAQ item 3 cites clm:1 to clm:4 but not clm:8. It says state law lists conditions that can make a building substandard, such as "junk and debris that are fire, health or safety hazards", with no threshold. H&S 17920.3 applies only where a listed condition exists "to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of the occupants of the building, nearby residents, or the public". The ledger notes on clm:1 to clm:4 say the threshold is carried by clm:8 and that every citing unit must cite it. Cite clm:8 and add the threshold in plain words. Omitting it changes what a reader would believe, so reader_impact is changes.

FAQ item 4 has no ledger claim behind it. It names "the owner, a trustee, an executor or administrator, or several heirs who agree", which is a list of legal roles. It also states "Living in the house alone does not give you that authority", which is a legal conclusion. Neither is supported. Remove the list and that sentence. Keep "Only someone with legal authority to sign". Add that who that is depends on how title is held, and that the seller should confirm with an attorney or title company.

FAQ item 3 moves from state law to "the city or county" with no local claim. Add the exact phrase "local rules vary; check with your city or county" (SR-2) so a reader does not take the state list as the local rule.

FAQ item 2 opens with "Not always." This implies no legal duty to clean out, and no ledger claim supports that. Soften it to something like "There is no single answer; it depends on..." so it does not read as a legal conclusion.
